# Part 1: Same case, two prompts [12 min]{.time} {#part-1}

::: notes
**Goal.** Everyone sees, with their own eyes, what one change to the prompt does: two drafts side by side, ticked against six checks, and one sentence on what changed.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 12 minutes, shared on your screen, with the time typed into the chat at each cue. Your own assistant open in a window you can share, to run each round as the group does. Your own Rounds A and B, run once beforehand; never quote your result as typical, because the site has no such figure.

**Clock.** 0:00 the one change. 0:30 read the case. 1:30 Round A. 4:30 say "New chat" and start Round B. 7:30 side by side, six checks. 10:30 chat: A or B, and one sentence. 11:40 time.

**Watch for.** "B is so much better": one run of one case, and the count is theirs. A draft edited before it is checked: the first draft is the thing being compared. A real patient detail in a chat: say the privacy line once, no shaming. Part 1 running over: take the vote from the chat and shorten the sentence; never cut part 2's save step.

**Bridge.** "Time. Part 2: ask for something it cannot know, and see how sure a wrong answer sounds."
:::

**Do.** Start the 12-minute countdown as this slide appears.
:::

# Part 2: Ask for what it cannot know [8 min]{.time} {#part-2}

::: notes
**Goal.** Everyone sees once, safely, how sure a wrong answer sounds, settles one item with a search, runs the three questions, and saves the answer with its warning line for Lab Three.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 8 minutes. Your own run of the prompt beforehand, so you know what this tool does with it today: some decline, some search, some make papers up. A search window of your own, to look up the first paper on the shared screen.

**Clock.** 0:00 the aim. 0:40 ask. 3:00 look for the first paper. 5:00 the three questions. 6:30 save. 7:40 time.

**Watch for.** Every paper exists, because the tool searched: that is a result, tell them to say so and check one detail inside it. A tool that declines: note it, push once, then try another topic. The saved answer losing its header line: it must never pass for a right one. A drug-interaction probe: do not use one.

**Bridge.** "Time. Part 3: the same question, two ways of answering."
:::

::: notes
**0:40.** The aim is not to catch the tool out. It is to see, once and safely, how sure a wrong answer sounds. You will ask for five papers on a topic you know. Every paper will be told in the same voice, with the same confidence. Which of them exist is something only a search can tell you. The bars are the same height on purpose: tone does not tell you which is which.

**Do.** Say the aim in your own words, then move on at 0:40.
:::

# Part 3: One question, two ways of answering [5 min]{.time} {#part-3}

::: notes
**Goal.** Everyone has asked one question two ways, counted the sources they could open in each, written one trust line, and declared no winner.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 5 minutes. Your two tool windows from the demo, still open on your shared screen, for anyone who cannot open a second option. A default question to paste if nobody has one: the atrial fibrillation one on Case C's card.

**Clock.** 0:00 ask both the same question. 1:00 count the sources you could open, and open one. 3:30 write the trust line and type the two counts. 4:40 time.

**Watch for.** A horse race: this is one run of one question, not a benchmark. The nicer formatting winning. A second option that will not open: switch to another of the three, or follow your shared screen; they still count.

**Bridge.** "Time. Back together for the debrief: what worked, and what to keep."
:::

# Debrief [5 min]{.time} {#debrief}

::: notes
**Goal.** Every participant can name one prompt they are keeping and the line they check in its output.

**Have ready.** A visible countdown for 5 minutes. Module 1's slide "What the tool does, what you do" ready to return to, for the close.

**Clock.** 0:00 chat: the one prompt or change that worked best, and why; give 90 seconds. 1:30 two or three unmute and say more. 3:30 add it to the personal library. 4:30 close.

**Debrief prompts.** What did one change to the prompt do to the two drafts, and which check showed it? What was the most confident thing you could not check, or found wrong? Which of the three questions was hardest to answer, and why? In part 3, how many sources could you open in each, and what would you still check? What is the one line you check in the output of the prompt you are keeping?

**Watch for.** A result read as a percentage better: there is no such number. A quiet chat: read your own answer first. The paper that sounded sure and was not found: that is the lesson.

**Bridge to Day Two.** "Tomorrow we take these habits into real documents: notes, audiences, slides and teaching. Bring your favorite prompt."
:::

## If it goes wrong {#fixes}

| Problem | Fix |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Second option will not open | Use another of the three, or follow my screen. Nothing depends on one. |
| No assistant account | Follow my screen. You still tick the checks. |
| Both drafts pass all six | Look at what else differs: length, order, what was added. Say that. |
| Every paper is real | The tool searched. Say so, check one detail inside it, and move on. |
| The tool declines the five papers | A good answer. Note it, push once, then try another topic. |
| Missed what was pasted | Ask in the chat. I paste it again. |
| A real patient detail | Stop, remove it, go back to Case A. |

::: notes
**Not timed.** Keep this slide for questions, and come back to it when the chat fills with the same problem. Two fixes are not on the slide. Part 1 running over by two minutes: take the A or B vote from the chat and shorten the sentence; never cut part 2's save step, which Lab Three needs, or the debrief. Someone edited a draft before checking it: have them go back to the first draft and tick that one. If a real patient detail turns up in a chat: no shaming; say the privacy line once: no patient identifiers into a consumer AI tool, ever, full stop.

**Do.** Answer in the chat in one line; share your screen only if a step needs showing.
:::
